sources.title: M. W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups, author manuscript of the first edition (Princeton University Press, 2008; 600 PDF pages)
sources.locator: Section 7.1 pp. 123-126 (Definition 7.1.1; the poset WS of spherical cosets (7.1); Examples 7.1.2-7.1.4; Lemma 7.1.9); section 7.2 pp. 126-127 (order complex |P| of a poset; K=|S|; Lemma 7.2.2; Lemma 7.2.3; Theorem 7.2.4); section 7.3 pp. 128-131 (Definition 7.3.1; Examples 7.3.2 and 7.3.6; Lemma 7.3.3 with proof; the General Case paragraph; Proposition 7.3.4; Lemma 7.3.5); section 7.4, Example 7.4.1, printed p. 132 (the universal Coxeter Davis tree); Notes, p. 135; Theorem 4.1.6(iii) as quoted in section 7.1; and section 2.2 pp. 19-20 (Cayley 2-complex of a presentation, Proposition 2.2.3). Not read for this batch: chapters 8-17, Appendices A-G, and the parts of chapters 4 and 6 outside the quoted clauses.

contents.name: Definition 7.1.1 (spherical subsets; the poset S of spherical subsets)
(7.1) the poset WS of spherical cosets, the projection WS -> S and the natural W-action with quotient poset S
Theorem 4.1.6(iii) (equality and inclusion of special cosets), quoted and used in section 7.1
Example 7.1.3 (the infinite dihedral group has nerve two points)
Example 7.4.1 (the universal Coxeter system has discrete nerve, free product of k copies of C_2, and a regular k-valent Davis tree)
Lemma 7.1.9 (W-finite mirror structures and the nerve) and Example 7.1.4 (geometric reflection groups)
contents.reason: The statement concerns general mirrored spaces and the construction of arbitrary right-angled examples; this pair needs neither the W-finiteness criterion for mirror structures nor the embedding of arbitrary cell complexes as nerves.

contents.name: Lemma 7.2.2 (every convex cell complex is the nerve of a right-angled Coxeter system) and Lemma 7.2.5
contents.reason: Both are existence/contractibility statements about nerves of general complexes; the pair constructs the Davis complex for a given Coxeter system and needs no nerve-realisation theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 7.2.3 (every simplex of Sigma is a translate of a chamber simplex)
Theorem 7.2.4 (Sigma is W-equivariantly homeomorphic to U(W,K))
Definition 7.3.1 (Coxeter polytope conv(Wx) for a generic point x) and the paragraph 'Coxeter Polytopes'
Examples 7.3.2(i) (C_2 gives an interval)
Examples 7.3.2(ii) (D_m gives a 2m-gon)
Example 7.3.6 (right-angled Coxeter systems have cubical Davis cells; B4 is the one-dimensional universal case)
Examples 7.3.2(iii)-(iv) (products, cubes for (C_2)^n, permutohedra for A_n)
Lemma 7.3.3 and its proof (face poset of the Coxeter polytope is the poset of special cosets; Dirichlet-domain supporting-hyperplane argument)
The paragraph 'The General Case' before Proposition 7.3.4 (the poset of cells of the type-W_T cell is W_T(S_{<=T}); cell structure coarser than the simplicial one)
Proposition 7.3.4 (cells are the spherical cosets; 0-skeleton W; 1-skeleton the Cayley graph; 2-skeleton a Cayley 2-complex; vertex link L)
Lemma 7.3.5 (Sigma is simply connected)
Section 2.2, Proposition 2.2.3 and Example 2.2.2 (Cayley 2-complex of a presentation, its cells and simple connectivity)
Notes, p. 135 (the cellulation is due to Moussong; the name Davis-Moussong/Davis complex)
contents.reason: Bibliographic attribution only; it carries no mathematical assertion and no proof input for this pair.

contents.name: The observation 'If W is finite, then Sigma is a Coxeter zonotope' (used in the dual-construction discussion)
Example 7.3.2(ii), the finite dihedral orbit polygon is regular when the generating point is equidistant from the sector rays
Section 2.2, Cayley 2-complex convention excluding relators s and s^2 from the attached 2-cells

contents.name: Definition 1.3.1 (a spherical coset; WS = union over spherical T of W/W_T)
Lemma 1.3.2 (wW_U is contained in vW_T iff w^{-1}v in W_T and U contained in T; citing Davis 4.1.6(iii))
Definition 1.3.3 (geometric realisation of a poset via Flag(P))
Definition 1.3.4 (the Davis complex as the geometric realisation of WS; p-simplex for a chain of p+1 spherical cosets)
Example 1.3.5 (W(I_2(3)) = D_6: the 13 spherical cosets, 0- and 1-simplices and 2-simplices of the Davis complex, and the action of s and t)
The paragraph after Definition 1.3.4 (W acts on WS by left multiplication; the quotient poset is S)
Lemma 1.2.13 (a finite Coxeter group has a unique longest element; spherical parabolics have longest elements)
Chapters 2-4 (second and third integral homology; homological stability for Artin monoids)
contents.reason: These chapters compute homology of Coxeter and Artin groups; the pair only needs the construction and incidence of the Davis complex, not its (co)homology.

sources.locator: PDF pp. 12-19: slides 'Second realization: the cell complex Sigma', 'Filling in Cay(W,S)', 'Coxeter zonotopes', 'Geometric realization of a poset', 'The dual construction of Sigma', 'Properties of this cell structure on Sigma', 'More properties', 'Relationship with geometric reflection groups'. The earlier slides on geometric reflection groups and the Tits representation were read only as background.

contents.name: Slide 'Coxeter zonotopes' (P_T is the convex hull of W_T x for x in the open fundamental cone; cubes when W_T = (Z/2)^n)
Slide 'Filling in Cay(W,S)' (polygons spanned by cosets of finite dihedral parabolics; filling them makes the 2-skeleton simply connected)

Slides 'Properties of this cell structure on Sigma' and 'More properties' (cells = WS; one W-orbit per spherical T; 0-skeleton W; 1-skeleton Cayley graph; 2-skeleton Cayley 2-complex; proper action with isotropy conjugate to spherical W_T; compact quotient; finite W gives a Coxeter zonotope)
Slide 'The dual construction of Sigma' (K = |S| is the cone on the barycentric subdivision of L; Sigma = U(W,K); K homeomorphic to Sigma/W)
Slides 'Moussong: the induced piecewise Euclidean metric on Sigma is CAT(0)' and 'Sigma is contractible'
contents.reason: The CAT(0) metric and contractibility of the Davis complex form the subject of the later CAT(0) pair, which is planned but not yet authored; this pair only supplies the cellulation, incidence and simple connectivity used there.

contents.name: Slide 'Relationship with geometric reflection groups' (K the fundamental polytope; the cell structure dual to the tessellation for Euclidean/hyperbolic reflection groups)
contents.reason: The comparison with geometric reflection groups on Euclidean and hyperbolic space is not needed for the abstract Davis complex construction of this pair.
